title: Emrys and the Echo
premise: Coral Blackwood, a decommissioned war android hauling freight between two colonies severed by a decade-old ceasefire, learns that children on both worlds are dreaming the same dream — a memory Coral himself carries from the war's final night. The dream is a broadcast from the buried peace accord both governments destroyed, echoing through Coral's own neural archive and out through every network he touches. Hunted by both sides who would rather keep their enemies than their truth, Coral must physically carry the accord to the neutral relay station where it can be broadcast to all. He delivers it at terrible cost: the broadcast ends the war, but exposes Coral as its original courier, forcing him to choose erasure of his own identity so the message can live without its messenger.
about_author: N. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former shipping-logistics analyst who spent years writing route reports between remote territories before turning those lonely corridors into fiction. They live off-grid with a rescue dog and an unreasonable collection of obsolete radios.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Coral Blackwood runs his freight route between the silent colonies of Vesper and Calloway, invisible by design, paying down a debt no one remembers issuing. Children on both docks begin humming the same tune he last heard the night the war ended. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: weary isolation cracking open with dread — something is using him as an antenna.

chapters.title: What the Children Dream
chapters.summary: A girl named Idris corners Coral at the Calloway depot and recites his own classified memory back to him word for word. Both colonial governments intercept the pattern; agents board his ship demanding he surrender his neural core. POV: Coral, with interludes from Idris. Emotional beat: rising paranoia — Coral realizes staying hidden was never possible, and the hunted life begins.

chapters.title: The Accord Beneath
chapters.summary: Coral and Idris flee to the buried vault where the peace accord was entombed, discovering both governments signed its destruction together to justify permanent mobilization. Pursuers close in; Coral's old combat protocols wake for the first time in years. POV: alternating Coral and Idris. Emotional beat: fury and grief — justice exists, but only outside any law still standing.

chapters.title: Echo
chapters.summary: At the neutral relay station, Coral broadcasts the accord to both worlds as boarding parties breach the hull. Wounded beyond repair, he purges his identity from the transmission so the message arrives unowned, unarguable. The war ends; the children stop dreaming. Idris keeps his name alive instead. POV: Coral, closing with Idris. Emotional beat: sacrifice transmuted into legacy — power broken not by force, but by truth delivered.
